sentences.text: Revenue compounded from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $332 billion in FY2026, a 14.7% CAGR [F1][F10][F221].
Operating income grew faster at a 20.5% CAGR [F223], lifting operating margin from 30.1% to 46.8% [F41][F50].
The FY2018 inflection was a tax event: net income fell 35.0% [D48] with a 54.6% effective tax rate [D32], which the filing attributes to the net charge from enactment of the TCJA [P61].
Growth slowed to 6.9% in FY2023 [D311] as More Personal Computing revenue fell 8.7% [D932], which the filing ties to Windows and Devices [P39].
FY2026 revenue growth reaccelerated to 17.8% [D472], driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud [P17].
Microsoft Cloud contributed 16.2pp of FY2026's 17.8% revenue growth and reached 64.6% of revenue [D568][D472][D566].
Server products and cloud services grew 31.5%, adding 11.0pp [D641][D642], because Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 41% [P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services grew 16.2%, adding 5.1pp [D648][D649], with revenue per user rising on Microsoft 365 Copilot and E5 [P14].
XBOX revenue fell 7.1% [D712], which the filing attributes to lower content and services revenue and a 29% drop in hardware on lower console volume [P10].
Operating leverage was positive: revenue growth beat operating-cost growth by 10.3pp and the incremental operating margin was 53.3% [D499][D498].
Diluted EPS compounded at 20.9% against 20.2% for net income, as diluted shares fell from 7,832 million to 7,453 million [F226][F224][X128][X137].
Operating margin of 46.8% is the window high, against a 41.7% median and a 30.1% low [F50][D974][D975][D973].
In FY2026 operating margin rose 1.2pp [D487] even though cost of revenue cut 0.9pp [D500], as gross margin fell to 67.9% [F30] on continued investment in AI infrastructure [P11].
R&D added 0.8pp and other lines added 1.2pp [D501][D502], with selling and marketing down to 8.0% of revenue from 16.1% in FY2017 [D451][D3].
The largest move was FY2021's 4.6pp gain [D220], where cost of revenue added 1.1pp [D232] and the filing cites a change in estimated useful lives of server and network equipment [P51].

Net margin of 40.3% was 6.5pp below operating margin of 46.8% [F70][F50], after other income of $10.7 billion [X124] that included $6.5 billion of OpenAI net gains, mainly a dilution gain from the recapitalization [P7].
The effective tax rate rose to 19.4% from 17.6% [D458][D404] on changes in the mix of US and foreign earnings [P5].
Operating cash flow rose 34.4% to $183 billion [D477][F100], on higher cash received from customers and less cash paid for income taxes [P1].
Free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion [D478][F120], only 0.50x net income, the window low against a 0.91x median [D460][D988][D990].
Capex reached $116 billion, 34.9% of revenue and 3.38x D&A [F110][D455][D461], as additions to property and equipment rose $51.4 billion [P1].
Free cash flow margin of 20.2% is the window low against a 30.3% median [D456][D982][D984].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, up from $66.8 billion, with cash and investments of $113 billion against $40.3 billion of debt [D465][D411][D463][D464].
Net cash at 22.0% of revenue ranks in the 83rd percentile of six software peers, whose median is -7.2% [D466][D1006][D1007].
The current ratio of 1.23x is the window low, against a 1.93x median [F200][D991][D993].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion and dividends of $26.4 billion totalled $48.7 billion, or 72.7% of free cash flow [X147][X157][D467][D468].
The diluted share count fell only 0.2% [D493], while long-term debt fell 22.6% [D483].
R1, free cash flow below 80% of net income, has persisted two years at 0.70x in FY2025 and 0.50x in FY2026 [R1][D406][D460].
The cause is the capex surge [P1], so earnings are converting to cash less than before, and the return on that spend is not yet visible in the cited figures [D455].
Net income grew 31.3% in FY2026 against 20.8% for operating income, helped by $6.5 billion of OpenAI net gains [D474][D473][P7].
Those gains are investment marks rather than operations, so net income overstates the earnings run-rate [X124].
The current ratio fell to 1.23x as current liabilities grew 19.5% [F200][D485].
Liquidity is thinner than at any point in the window, though net cash stays positive [D991][D465].
Data check: FY2017 pretax income and tax are first-reported values later recast, and FY2026 product revenue members overlap [R2][R3][R5].
Conclusions here avoid FY2017 tax comparisons and do not add up product lines [X95][X105].
Free cash flow to net income falling below 0.50x would confirm worsening conversion, and recovery toward the 0.91x median would reverse it [D460][D990]; both appear in the FY2027 10-K.
Capex to D&A staying above 3.38x [D461] would show the build-out still outrunning depreciation, while a decline would signal the intensity peaking, in the FY2027 10-K.
Gross margin below 67.9% [F30] would suggest AI infrastructure costs are outpacing pricing, while a rise above it would reverse that, in the FY2027 10-K.
A current ratio below the 1.23x window low [D991] would extend the liquidity squeeze, as shown in the FY2027 10-K.
